_comment: One source for every host manifest. Adding a host is an entry here, not a hand-edited tree. Regenerate with `godmode bindings --write`; `--check` fails when a manifest has drifted from this file.

identity.name: godmode
identity.description: A local, tamper-evident record of what a coding agent did, what it claimed, and what was verified.

claude.note: hooks/hooks.json is loaded by convention; declaring a hooks key causes a duplicate-load error

extra.description: Skills for a local, tamper-evident record of what a coding agent did, what it claimed, and what was verified.

interface.shortDescription: Local continuity and guarded coding workflows.
interface.longDescription: Godmode reconstructs repository reality from local evidence, preserves private continuity, diagnoses failures without looping, previews protected actions, and can forge validated project skills when a reusable gap is proven.
defaultPrompt: Resume this repository from verified local context.
Diagnose this failure without repeating failed hypotheses.
Preview this protected action and its recovery path.

hook_manifests._comment: CX-3: per-host HOOK artifacts (distinct from the identity manifests above). Content is built by scripts/godmode_runtime/godmode_host_manifests.py's HOOK_ARTIFACTS registry - this section supplies only the PATH each host's artifact is written to, the same division of labour `hosts` above already uses (path here, content generation in code). `godmode bindings --write`/`--check` drive both sections from one command. Codex's build doc and Grok's 09-plugins.md both name ./hooks/hooks.json as the one hooks file a plugin carries - the SAME default path Claude loads - so codex and grok are merge-into-shared: their tool names join that file's PreToolUse matcher and its entries are shell-form command strings every host parses (2026-08-28 field reports: Grok resolved a bare `python` token against the file's directory, Codex refused the args shape). cursor/gemini keep a dedicated file because their envelopes (`version: 1`/`failClosed`; settings fragment) differ in shape, not only in path.

adapters._comment: Instruction-file adapters for hosts without a plugin manifest. Controls state what each host can actually hold; the adapter docs must match this matrix (tests enforce agreement).

why.interactive_authorization: OpenCode's permission model (ask/allow/deny per tool) prompts the user outside model judgment
why.tool_call_interception: a Bun plugin shim ships (adapters/opencode/godmode.opencode.js): OpenCode's documented `tool.execute.before` throw stops the tool, and the shim throws on every gate deny, on `ask` (folded to deny with the staged-capability remedy), on a missing interpreter and on a missing root - fail-closed. SOFT, not HARD, until a live OpenCode session's block is chronicled as a proof

why.interactive_authorization: auto-run settings can bypass the prompt, so the prompt cannot be counted on
why.tool_call_interception: project rules are advisory text; no pre-tool boundary is exposed

why.interactive_authorization: approval mode confirms mutations outside model judgment unless the operator enables auto-approval
why.tool_call_interception: GEMINI.md context is advisory; no pre-tool boundary is exposed
